Public Healthcare Facilities in Puri District, Odisha
A Structured Reference Guide to District, Community, and Primary Health Facilities
Overview
Puri district, best known as the seat of the Jagannath Temple and a major pilgrimage and coastal destination, is served by a tiered public healthcare network under the Odisha Department of Health & Family Welfare, coordinated locally by the Chief District Medical Officer (CDMO), Puri. The system follows the standard national structure: village-level Sub-Centres feed into Primary Health Centres (PHCs), which refer upward to Community Health Centres (CHCs) at the block level, which in turn refer to the District Headquarters Hospital (DHH) as the district's main secondary-level referral point. Puri city is also home to Shri Jagannath Medical College and Hospital (SJMCH), a government medical college established in 2021, which adds a tertiary-care teaching hospital tier above the DHH. This overall structure follows the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS), issued by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) through the National Health Mission (NHM) and most recently revised in 2022.
Facility Types
District Headquarters Hospital (DHH), Puri
DHH Puri, originally known as the Puri Pilgrimage Hospital, was rebuilt in 1909-10 and remains one of the district's oldest and most established public health institutions. It has the distinction of being among the first district hospitals in Odisha, and the second in India, to receive ISO 9001:2008 quality management certification. As the district's secondary-level referral hospital, it is designed to receive cases referred from CHCs, PHCs, and Sub-Centres across all of Puri district's blocks, and given the district's high pilgrim and tourist footfall, it also plays an important role in handling visitor health emergencies alongside routine district referral care.
Community Health Centres (CHCs)
CHCs are block-level referral units, generally serving a population of roughly 80,000 to 120,000 people. Puri district's blocks — including Kanas, Gop, Chandanpur/Nimapara area, Brahmagiri, Satyabadi, Astaranga, Delanga, Pipili, and others — each have a CHC that acts as the referral hub for the PHCs and Sub-Centres within that block. For example, CHC Kanas, established in 1962, is a 24x7 facility (non-FRU) overseeing five PHCs and twenty-three Sub-Centres in its block, and is ISO 9001:2015 certified, illustrating the level of service standardization found at some CHCs in the district. A CHC is expected to have around 30 inpatient beds, an operation theatre, basic diagnostic and blood storage facilities, and specialist coverage in medicine, surgery, obstetrics/gynaecology, and paediatrics, though actual staffing varies by centre; centres equipped for round-the-clock emergency obstetric and newborn care may be designated First Referral Units (FRUs).
Primary Health Centres (PHCs)
PHCs are typically the first point of contact with a qualified doctor for rural and semi-urban residents, each covering a population of around 20,000 to 30,000. Puri district has numerous PHCs and newer PHC(New) facilities distributed across its blocks — for instance, Astaranga block alone has several PHC(New) units in addition to its main PHC. Each PHC supervises a cluster of Sub-Centres, provides outpatient consultation, a small number of inpatient beds, basic laboratory testing, and normal delivery services at PHCs designated for 24x7 care, and oversees ASHA and ANM workers at the village level.
Sub-Centres and Health & Wellness Centres
Below the PHC level, Health Sub-Centres — increasingly upgraded as Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres (AB-HWCs) — are the most peripheral public facilities, generally staffed by an ANM and a Community Health Officer. They handle preventive and promotive care such as immunization and antenatal check-ups, referring more complex cases upward to the PHC.
What Each Facility Handles
District Headquarters Hospital
Complex and emergency cases referred from CHCs and PHCs across the district
Broader specialist consultation and surgical services than block-level facilities
Diagnostics, blood storage/blood bank services, and larger inpatient bed capacity
Emergency care for pilgrims and tourists visiting Puri, alongside routine district referral cases
Possible empanelment under schemes such as Ayushman Bharat–PM-JAY for cashless treatment (current empanelment status should be verified locally)
Acts as the secondary-level referral hospital for the district, with onward referral to Shri Jagannath Medical College and Hospital or another tertiary centre for cases needing higher-level specialty care
Community Health Centres
Referral care for PHCs and Sub-Centres within the block, plus specialist consultation for patients approaching directly
Inpatient care (around 30 beds at fully staffed centres), minor and some major surgical procedures, and operation theatre services
Emergency obstetric care and institutional deliveries, particularly at 24x7-designated centres
Basic diagnostics including laboratory services and, at many centres, X-ray facilities
Primary Health Centres
Outpatient consultation for common illnesses, minor injuries, and chronic disease follow-up
Antenatal, natal, and postnatal care, including normal deliveries at 24x7 PHCs
Immunization, family planning services, and national health programme delivery (TB, malaria, non-communicable disease screening, and similar)
Basic laboratory tests (blood, urine, blood sugar, malaria rapid tests, and similar)
First-level stabilization and referral of serious cases to a CHC or the District Headquarters Hospital
How to Reach Them (General Guidance)
Since exact addresses and phone numbers are not being invented here, the following general approaches can help locate and reach the correct facility:
Ask the local ASHA worker, ANM, or Anganwadi worker — they know the nearest Sub-Centre and PHC serving a household and can help with referral upward if needed.
Every block headquarters in Puri district has a CHC (for example, Kanas, Gop, Chandanpur, Brahmagiri); the block administrative office can confirm its exact current location and status.
The Puri district administration's official website and the CDMO Puri office maintain listings of health facilities; these should be treated as the authoritative source for confirmed addresses and phone numbers.
The National Health Mission (NHM) Odisha and Odisha Directorate of Health Services websites publish facility directories and health scheme information at the state level.
The 108 (emergency response) and 102 (patient transport / maternal-child) ambulance services can be used to reach an appropriate facility in an emergency, and can also help route a patient to the correct level of care.
For the District Headquarters Hospital specifically, and to distinguish it from Shri Jagannath Medical College and Hospital located separately in Puri city, confirm the current address and scope of services with the district health administration before travelling.
Given Puri's high pilgrim and tourist traffic, visitors unfamiliar with the area should ask local authorities, hotel staff, or temple administration for the nearest functioning public health facility in an emergency.
When to Go to District Hospital vs PHC
Go to a PHC (or Sub-Centre) first for:
Routine illnesses — fever, cold, minor infections, common ailments
Antenatal check-ups, immunizations, and family planning services
Normal, uncomplicated deliveries at a 24x7-designated PHC
Basic diagnostic tests and follow-up for chronic conditions already under management
Minor injuries and first-aid level care
Go to (or be referred to) a CHC for:
Cases needing minor surgery, specialist consultation, or inpatient observation beyond what a PHC can provide
Complicated deliveries or emergency obstetric care, especially at a 24x7 or FRU-designated CHC
Situations where the PHC has stabilized a patient but recommended referral
Go directly to the District Headquarters Hospital for:
Serious emergencies — major trauma, accidents, severe medical emergencies where higher-level care is clearly needed
Conditions requiring specialist care, surgery, or diagnostics not available at PHC or CHC level
Cases already referred by a PHC or CHC as needing secondary-level hospital care
Health emergencies during pilgrimage seasons or large public gatherings, when DHH Puri is typically better equipped to handle higher patient volumes than a PHC
Situations covered under empanelled schemes (e.g., PM-JAY) requiring hospital-level admission — confirm current scheme coverage locally
As a general rule, the public health system is designed as a step-up referral chain: Sub-Centre → PHC → CHC → District Headquarters Hospital → Medical College Hospital, with each level equipped for progressively more complex care. In Puri's case, DHH's long-established role and ISO certification make it a strong first stop for most secondary-level care, with Shri Jagannath Medical College and Hospital available for cases needing tertiary or specialized attention. Bypassing lower tiers is appropriate mainly in genuine emergencies, where reaching the nearest capable facility quickly — often via 108 ambulance services — matters more than following the tier order.

Note: This document is a general reference compiled from the sources above. All facility-specific contact details, current staffing, and addresses should be verified with the CDMO Puri office or the Odisha Directorate of Health Services before being treated as final.
⚠ IMPORTANT NOTE ON CONTACT DETAILS
This document describes facility types, functions, and general navigation guidance only. Exact phone numbers, office addresses, named officers, and facility-specific contact details are placeholders to be filled in later using official information obtained directly from the Puri District Health Office / CDMO Puri, the Odisha Directorate of Health Services, or the National Health Mission (NHM) Odisha website. No phone numbers or addresses have been invented for this document; where specifics are not confirmed, that is stated explicitly rather than guessed.
